models_evaluated: four blinded AI systems (others not named)

links.outcome: Oncologist-rated utility and trust of AI literature reports under different report designs
links.effect: Evidence-graded report rated lower in overall utility than standard OpenEvidence despite similar references (mean difference -0.96; 95% CI -1.26 to -0.66; P<.001).
links.quote: Evidence presented differently can alter perceptions of clinical utility and trust; accuracy alone is insufficient, and report design must also be empirically evaluated.

links.outcome: Factors reducing clinician trust in AI-generated literature reports, including citation problems
links.effect: Qualitative analysis found trust deteriorated with citation mismatch, buried provenance, evidence misclassification, overconfident recommendations, and poor organization.
links.quote: Trust deteriorated with citation mismatch, buried provenance, evidence misclassification, overconfident recommendations, and poor organization.

unlisted_practices: Designing AI literature-review reports as concise, scannable summaries with quantitative outcomes and recognizable bolded guidelines
Evidence-grading of cited sources within AI reports

screen.reason: Evaluates clinician preferences and trust across different AI presentation formats (e.g., standard vs. evidence-graded reporting and citation presentation) using clinical vignettes.

primary.practice: evidence report formatting and verification design
